filename_guards.name: traversal uid must not become a filename
uid with a slash must not become a filename
dotdot uid must not become a filename
empty uid must not become a filename

flag.name: non-standard NaN must be rejected identically in both languages
schema_version true must NOT enable (Python bool==1 divergence)
schema_version 1.0 enables — JSON has one number type, so both languages must agree
flag.note: Python can distinguish 1.0 from 1; JavaScript cannot. The strictest implementable shared rule is: numeric 1, never boolean.

null title falls back to bare uid
federated uid keeps its whole shape as the suffix

governed_filename.title: already-slugged-title

guards.name: a uid containing a path separator is refused
a uid with a dot is refused
a home outside the governed allowlist is refused
an arbitrary directory as home is refused even if it exists
a valid bare uid and a declared home do not raise
a valid federated uid does not raise

note: The single behavioural source for governed filename slugging, shared by vault/tools/lib/governed_path.py and tropo-app/lib/governed-path.ts. Neither implementation is the other's oracle; both execute THIS. Dev-spec 74f85939. Rules: lowercase; spaces/underscores to '-'; drop anything outside [a-z0-9-]; collapse and trim hyphens; truncate to 60 chars at a word boundary, hard-truncating if no boundary exists at or before 60 and trimming any trailing hyphen; empty output is null.

resolve.name: bare uid file resolves
readable file resolves by anchored suffix
a rename still resolves — the whole point of the fallback
exact and slugged both claiming one uid is AMBIGUOUS, bare does not win
resolve.note: Argus A145: letting the bare name win is a silent choice wearing a rule.

resolve.name: resolves in a non-files governed home
unanchored suffix must NOT match — xxxx<uid>.md is a different file
a uid that is a substring of another uid does not match it
absent uid returns null
federated uid resolves as a whole anchored suffix
a federated uid is not matched by its bare tail
two readable files claiming one uid is ambiguous and fails loudly
literal path is used when it exists and its frontmatter uid matches
a literal path whose frontmatter uid disagrees is ignored, not trusted
a literal path that does not exist falls through to the scan
home restricts the search
non-markdown files with a matching stem are ignored
unanchored stem whose frontmatter DOES claim the uid must still not match
resolve.note: The discriminating case for anchoring. Every other negative is also refused by the frontmatter check, so an unanchored glob passes them. Here the frontmatter agrees and only the missing hyphen anchor can reject it.

resolve.name: exact <uid>.md whose frontmatter declares a DIFFERENT uid is not a match
resolve.note: P0-1. The exact path skipped frontmatter verification entirely.

files.vault/files/gg000002.md:
---
uid: gg000002
body with no closing fence

resolve.name: exact <uid>.md with UNCLOSED frontmatter is not a match
resolve.note: An unterminated --- block is a truncated file, not frontmatter.

resolve.name: slugged file with UNCLOSED frontmatter is not a match
file with no frontmatter at all is not a match
cross-home collision is AMBIGUOUS, first home does not win
resolve.note: P1-1. vault/files is searched before vault/agents; both must count.

resolve.name: an absolute literal outside every governed home is refused, not read
resolve.note: P0-2 local-file-disclosure. The literal is the caller-controlled input.

resolve.name: a four-hyphen opening line does not open frontmatter
a closing line with trailing junk does not close frontmatter
a proper closed fence resolves (the control for the two above)
literal joins the candidate set — a literal plus a colliding scan hit is AMBIGUOUS
resolve.note: The literal must not short-circuit collision detection.
